title: Nigeria Wants to End Rabies by 2030. Here's What That Means for Your Next Dog.
body:
Nigeria is working with international partners toward eliminating rabies by 2030, with authorities outlining plans for a mass dog vaccination campaign, Tribune reported this week. It's a quiet kind of news, the sort that rarely comes up in everyday conversation, but it says something worth sitting with: enough dogs have gone unvaccinated for long enough that a national campaign is now considered necessary.

Rabies isn't something most dog owners think about day to day, especially a dog that mostly stays close to a familiar compound. But the usual story behind a rabies case is almost always the same: a bite from an unvaccinated, unfamiliar animal, often in a household where a vet visit got postponed or never came up at all. A national campaign works at the scale of a whole country. A single household's habits are what actually close that gap at the scale of one dog and one family.

That's worth sitting with if you're in the middle of finding a dog or a cat right now, whether on PetMatch or anywhere else. A listing, a WhatsApp message, or a friend's recommendation can tell you a pet looks healthy and friendly. None of that is the same as an actual vaccination record, and none of it is something PetMatch, or any free directory built the same way, independently checks. Listings here are self-reported by the person who posted them, which is exactly why the checking has to happen in person, not on the strength of a message thread.

So treat it as a normal, unremarkable part of meeting a match: ask to see vaccination records before anything is final, and if a pet hasn't had its rabies shot yet, make that the next stop rather than an afterthought. It costs almost nothing to ask, and it's the difference between hoping a new dog is protected and actually knowing. More on meeting another owner safely, including what to check before any pairing, is at https://petmatch.fit/safety.
link_label: Tribune: Nigeria seeks collaboration to eliminate rabies in 2030, plans mass dog vaccination
